name: Ramp
text: Add a single high-contrast skip link at the top of every page. It’s the fastest way to let keyboard users bypass repetitive blocks like headers and nav bars, cutting navigation time from seconds to a single keystroke. The trade-off is one extra link in the DOM, but it’s invisible to mouse users and adds negligible weight.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is a persistent skip link in the top-left corner clutters the viewport for sighted keyboard users—it’s always visible, even when unnecessary. A better alternative is a skip link that only appears after the first tab press, then hides until the next page load, balancing discoverability and clutter. Settle it with a quick A/B test: measure time-to-task for keyboard users with both versions.
